device.category: 4-voice analogue polyphonic synthesizer, 37 slim keys with polyphonic aftertouch
device.based_on: Prophet-5 voice architecture (envelope curves, rev 1/2 style filter) with a Pro-One style modulation section; released 2025.

architecture.polyphony_mode: 4-voice polyphonic with polyphonic aftertouch; unison 1-4 voices (with key priority) or chord memory
architecture.patch_memory_note: 512 programs: User Banks 1-2 (writable; U2 ships as 128 Basic Programs) and Factory Banks 1-2 (permanent), 128 each; sequences and chord memory saved per program; category browsing.
architecture.summary: Per voice: Oscillator A (saw and/or pulse, sync to B) and Oscillator B (triangle, saw and/or pulse; lo1/lo2 LFO ranges), 5-octave ranges and ±7 semitone fine tune, pulse widths in the Param menu; a mixer with noise (white, pink, violet) and a soft-clipping feedback path from the filter output; a 4-pole resonant low-pass (Prophet-5 rev 1/2 style, bass compensated) with filter ADSR, key tracking and velocity; an amp ADSR with velocity. A Pro-One style modulation section routes filter envelope, Osc B and LFO (any of saw, triangle, square, S/H at 0.021-556 Hz) through a direct bus or the Mod Wheel bus to eight destinations; an aftertouch section sends poly pressure to up to six. Unison, chord memory, hold, glide (4 modes), arpeggiator with 64-step note and mod sequencer, 65 alternative tunings.

modules.name: Keyboard and voice assigner
modules.description: 37-key Tactive keybed (velocity, poly aftertouch); 4 voices, unison 1-4 with key priority, chord memory, hold, glide, transpose ±2 octaves, alternative tunings.

modules.name: Oscillator A
modules.description: Analogue VCO: sawtooth and pulse, selectable together; hard sync to Osc B; 5-octave range, ±7 semitones fine.

modules.name: Oscillator B
modules.description: Analogue VCO: triangle, sawtooth and pulse, selectable together; lo1 (LFO range, key tracked) and lo2 (LFO range, no tracking); a modulation source.

modules.name: Mixer
modules.description: Osc A and Osc B levels, noise (on/level) and feedback (on/level) from the filter output through soft-clipping diodes.

modules.name: Filter
modules.description: 4-pole resonant low-pass after the Prophet-5 rev 1/2 design, with bass compensation; self-oscillates; key tracking quarter, half or full.

modules.name: Filter envelope
modules.description: ADSR (Prophet-5 response curves) to cutoff by ENV AMT (bipolar), with velocity; also a modulation source.

modules.name: Amp envelope
modules.description: ADSR to the VCA, with velocity.

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Voice amplifier under the amp envelope; a modulation and aftertouch destination.

modules.name: LFO
modules.description: 0.021-556 Hz or synced; saw (or reverse), triangle, square and S/H selectable together; S/H types S/H, random, pink, white, violet, DC. Monophonic.

modules.name: Modulation section
modules.description: Pro-One style: three sources (filter env, Osc B, LFO), each with an amount and a route (direct bus or Mod Wheel bus), to eight destinations each set to direct, Mod Wheel or both.

modules.name: Aftertouch section
modules.description: Poly pressure with one bipolar amount to up to six destinations (Freq A, Freq B, filter, amp, LFO freq, LFO amount) on three destination buttons.

modules.name: Arpeggiator and sequencer
modules.description: Arpeggiator (up, down, up+down 1/2, random, assign; 1-3 octaves; repeats; relatch; beat sync) and 64-step Seq Note / Seq Mod modes; 30-250 BPM, clock divisions, MIDI clock.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Mono main output and headphones; VOLUME (not stored) and program volume.

mod_matrix.name: Modulation section (Pro-One style, two buses)
mod_matrix.note: Each source's ROUTE button picks the direct bus (red) or the Mod Wheel bus (blue); each destination's button picks direct, Mod Wheel or both (purple). A source reaches every destination listening to its bus, at the source's single bipolar amount; the Mod Wheel bus is scaled by the wheel. The Mod Sequence reaches one destination chosen by Seq Mod Dest (including the three source amounts, PW A+B and feedback).

behaviours.name: Signal path
behaviours.rule: Per voice: oscillators, noise and feedback into the 4-pole low-pass, then the VCA under the amp ADSR; voices summed to the mono output. Feedback returns the filter output to its input through soft-clipping diodes.

behaviours.name: Modulation buses
behaviours.rule: Press a source ROUTE once for the direct bus (red), twice for the Mod Wheel bus (blue). Press a destination once for direct, twice for Mod Wheel, three times for both (purple). Mod Wheel bus modulation is heard only as the wheel rises, up to the source's amount.

behaviours.name: Osc B as modulator
behaviours.rule: lo1 keeps key tracking (a polyphonic, note-dependent LFO); lo2 disconnects it from the keyboard. Routed through the OSC B bus it gives per-voice modulation, or audio-rate FM in normal ranges.

behaviours.name: Polyphonic aftertouch
behaviours.rule: Per-key pressure (Tactive keybed) with one bipolar amount to up to six destinations on three buttons, each cycling first, second, both, off. LFO destinations are monophonic (the hardest key sets them). Global setting: off, mono or poly.

behaviours.name: Unison and chord memory
behaviours.rule: Unison stacks 1-4 voices with detune and key priority. Chord mode: hold a 2-4 note chord and press UNISON; single keys then play the transposed chord (saved with the program). HOLD sustains up to four notes at the amp sustain level.

behaviours.name: Arpeggiator and sequencer
behaviours.rule: Up, down, up+down 1/2, random, assign over 1-3 octaves with repeats, relatch and beat sync; 30-250 BPM or MIDI clock. Seq Note records up to 64 steps of notes or chords with rests, ties and note glides; Seq Mod records note numbers as mod amounts for one destination. Play modes: retrig, continue, one shot, step. Saved per program.

behaviours.name: Pedal input
behaviours.rule: Expression pedal (filter full/half, mod amounts, volume) or footswitch (sustain, arp hold, momentary hold, seq start/stop); trigger and gate modes also accept an audio signal to step the arpeggiator or gate the envelopes.

behaviours.name: Programs
behaviours.rule: 512 programs (User 1-2, Factory 1-2). Hold PROGRAM to save (factory edits go to a user bank). Live panel mode via Preset Mode off. Basic Program: TRANSPOSE down + PROGRAM. Category browsing. Entering the Global menu sets the power-on program.

source_inconsistencies: The power supply is 12 V 1.25 A, 15 W in the guide; retailers list 12 V 1.2 A and 14 W.
The guide calls the headphone output stereo; some retailer copy says mono (the signal path is mono).
Arp Repeat is described as '1, 2, 3' in one place and 'Off, 1, 2, 3' in another; Arp Octave in the Param list is given as '30-250' before '1, 2, 3'.
The aftertouch section mentions 'six possible parameters' including 'amp envelope amount', listed elsewhere as 'amp'.
One retailer lists DADSR envelopes; the guide describes ADSR.
The table of contents lists Polyphonic Aftertouch on page 35 after Unison on page 38, and repeats Unison and Hold.

modelling_gaps.detail: Voice modules are modelled once (per_voice); the LFO, buses and arpeggiator are common.
The modulation section is drawn as two buses feeding each destination per its button state; each source joins one bus by its ROUTE setting.
The guide mentions a Fourm Module (no keyboard); not modelled separately.
